about.title: Roshd — Khorasan Wind Pathfinder
about.lead: Roshd is a wind routing system built on real Khorasan station data — from data preprocessing to routing, delivered in one interface with both 2D and 3D views.
about.what1: Roshd takes wind observations from Khorasan weather stations, passes them through quality control (QC) and IDW/Kriging interpolation, and builds wind fields over four altitude bands from 1,500 to 3,600 m. These fields are the basis of every route the system computes — no synthetic data.
about.what2: The routing engine offers several algorithms: wind-aware A* (default), Dijkstra, Smoothed A* and Wind Riding. The optimization criterion is selectable — fastest, lowest energy or balanced — and operational constraints such as maximum wind speed and flight altitude band are applied directly in the settings.
about.what3: Results are presented in two views: an interactive 2D map with wind layers and a wind-resistance gradient along the route line, and a 3D scene with real terrain, wind vectors and a color-coded route tube. Each route reports distance, estimated time, selected altitude band and a wind-resistance profile.
about.fig1Caption: The route settings panel: optimization criterion, algorithm, altitude band and flight limits. The magnifier insets a close-up of the wind-resistance legend.
about.fig2Caption: The route line on the map with a wind-resistance gradient — white means flying with the wind, dark red means high resistance. Wind speed layers and vectors appear in the background.
about.fig3Caption: Real terrain with Lambert shading, the wind-vector field of the active altitude band, and the color-coded route tube based on wind resistance along the path.
about.how1: 1. Raw station data is fetched and kept in the cache.
about.how2: 2. Quality control screens out outlier and incomplete records.
about.how3: 3. IDW and Kriging interpolation build the wind field on a regular grid.
about.how4: 4. The routing engine finds the optimal path over the wind field and terrain using the selected algorithm.
about.how5: 5. The interface presents the route in both 2D and 3D views, with the wind-resistance indicator and flight details.
about.stackText: The user interface is built with React and TypeScript; the 2D map renders with MapLibre GL and the 3D scene with three.js. A small Python service in the background computes the wind fields and routes from station data.
about.dataText: The data in this version is an interpolation of Khorasan weather stations across four altitude bands (1,500, 2,200, 2,900 and 3,600 m). Roshd was built for research, proof of concept and field work by the project's Persian-speaking team.
about.fig4Title: Figure 4 — Wind resistance along the route
about.fig4Caption: How the route color changes: segments aligned with the wind stay white, and as resistance grows the color approaches dark red. The panel legend is built from the same ramp function.
